C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT.Summary: Document the cursor event protocol that the CLI already enforces inside skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md (and its packaged mirror): every kind in KNOWN_KIND_STATE, the terminal-before-fold rule (F12), and the attempt ordering constraint for honest red-first WriteEvidence (F9.8) — with a mechanical check against an exported kind set so the contract cannot silently fall behind the code (D11; F10 lesson).
C-EXECUTION-CONTRACT.Problem:
skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md is the execution contract handed to every coding agent that runs a GRACE change. The CLI enforces a protocol that skill does not fully state. Two gaps have already cost live work; the class is wider.
F12. Fold requires a terminal event inside each allocation (validateEventsAgainstAllocations in grace-cursor.ts: unterminated range when kind === "terminal" is missing). The skill mentions fold and epoch open, and never names terminal. Executors following the skill hit the wall at fold and paid a round trip. Emitting terminal remains an operator judgment (A29.2); the defect is missing instruction, not missing automation.
F9.8. Honest red-first recording requires cursor attempt --outcome fail written in its own round trip, before the production edit that follows. recordAttempt snapshots WriteEvidence at command time (snapshotWriteEvidence of ObservedWriteScope digests). An attempt recorded in the same tool batch as the fix digests a tree that already contains the fix, so ngrace review raises review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated and the ledger cannot corroborate the sequence. The skill never states this ordering. Disclosed five consecutive times by executors who knew red-first was required and still could not satisfy it, because nothing told them how.
D11 reversed the deferral of both to P1: topical filing is not justification; P1.10 would have written the same workflow words; P1 is unscheduled. They get this small bundle now (skills + a minimal kind-set export; see Constraints).
Class, not two paragraphs. KNOWN_KIND_STATE (grace-cursor.ts:267–278) defines nine event kinds (measured by parsing the const at HEAD 31d93bb; denominator 9 from that definition alone):
opened, progress, resume, attempt, verification-unavailable, command-run, pause, terminal, escalation
Semantic re-measure of the skill (not substring counts — F12.2): does the skill tell an agent when to emit each kind and what it means?
attempt — yes: dedicated command, outcomes, signatures, claimedConfidence, and ban on advance --kind attempt verification-unavailable — yes: when verification cannot run; never silence pause, resume — incidental English only ("pause/resume around interruptions"; recovery "resume or revert"; "paused-pending-approval" as state prose). Not named as event kinds with emit protocol. opened, progress, command-run, terminal, escalation — absent as protocol (escalation appears only as the verb "escalate to paused-pending-approval" after two failed attempts, not as kind=escalation)
**Of the 9 kinds, 2 are documented as protocol** (attempt, verification-unavailable). pause and resume are the incidental-English case: they appear as ordinary words, never as kind protocol. A substring scan finds at most 4 of 9 word hits — that figure is an **upper bound on mentions**, not a documentation score. A completeness check that counted substrings would score this contract 4 and be wrong; that is exactly the failure mode AC-KIND-COMPLETENESS-TIED-TO-CODE exists to make permanent. The contract omits most of the vocabulary it requires, including the kind mandatory to fold (terminal) and the kind that signals paused-pending-approval (escalation). command-run was added by C-CALIBRATION-COMMAND-EVIDENCE and documented nowhere — proof that a string-match "we wrote terminal once" fix will rot on the next kind.
F9.6 / F9.7 remain context: multi-task suite attribution and pass-only invisibility to the attempt-pair check. This bundle does not fix attribution schema; it documents the operational ordering F9.8 requires so executors can stop producing unsubstantiated pairs by accident.

Goals.Goal: Every kind in the exported known-kind set (lockstep with KNOWN_KIND_STATE) is documented in ngrace-execute as protocol — when to emit it, what it means for cursor state / lifecycle — not merely present as an incidental English word.
Terminal-before-fold is explicit: fold is blocked without a terminal inside the allocation; the operator emits terminal (A29.2); recover --fix does not.

F9.8 ordering is explicit with reason: fail attempt in its own round trip before the edit; digests snapshot at attempt time; batched fail+fix produces an unsubstantiated pair (review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated); an honest gap disclosed is cheap, a contradiction is not.

A mechanical regression imports the **exported** kind set from grace-cursor (not a source parse) and fails if any kind lacks a non-incidental documentation marker in the skill — so a tenth kind cannot ship silently undocumented. Precedent: C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY T-005 / F10 — parsing source for issue codes missed an entire namespace while looking sound; do not repeat that shape.
Canonical skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md and packaged plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md remain byte-identical (validate-marketplace drift check continues to pass).

Constraints.Constraint: Binding: D11; F12, F12.2, F9.8 (F9.6/F9.7 context only); A29.2 / F1 (binary does not invent terminals); P0.10 attempt-pair detection remains detection, not prevention; D5.5 (CHANGELOG.md is generated — never hand-edited; any release note for a later release act lives in the conventional-commit body).
Spec only until planned and approved (F4 two-stage). status remains "draft" in this pass; approval is a human act. Do not author plan.xml until the spec is approved.

Documentation of protocol the CLI already enforces, plus a **minimal** runtime export of the known-kind set (or a derived exhaustive list kept in lockstep with KNOWN_KIND_STATE) from src/grace-cursor.ts so the completeness check can import a definition rather than parse source (F10). Do not change cursor, gate, review, or fold behaviour beyond that export. Do not restructure ngrace-execute into a different skill shape (not P1.10 emphasis inversion). The export is as small as it can be — the kind set or derived list, nothing more.

Anticipated write scope: skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md, plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md, src/grace-cursor.ts (export only), and co-located tests that consume the export. AffectedAreas: M-SKILLS and M-CURSOR.

Sequencing with C-REPORT-HONESTY: that bundle's spec is already approved and claims M-CURSOR; its plan is not yet authored. This bundle is finished (spec → plan → execute) **before** C-REPORT-HONESTY's plan is authored, so the two never hold approved plans at once and no scope.durable-overlap arises. That ordering is the reason the shared M-CURSOR claim is safe; do not invert it. Do not modify C-REPORT-HONESTY or C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE directories.

Both skill trees always: edit canonical skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md and keep plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md synchronized in the same change. CLAUDE.md and scripts/validate-marketplace.ts require packaged-vs-canonical parity.

"Documented" for the completeness check must be mechanically checkable against the **exported** kind set and not satisfiable by an incidental English mention of the word "attempt" (or "pause", "resume", etc.). How that is marked (named heading, table row, explicit marker comment, structured block) is the plan's choice; the non-incidental property is binding.

This bundle does **not** touch any version surface: not package.json version, README packaged-version marker, openpackage.yml, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, or plugins/ngrace/.claude-plugin/plugin.json. Version surfaces belong to the deliberate release act (scripts/release-bump.ts takes an explicit semver target and updateVersionSurfaceFiles rewrites every surface at once); they are not derived from commit types and are not owned by change bundles. Hand-bumping here would collide with release:bump and with validate-marketplace's version-sync check. Measured across all 20 archived plans: zero declare marketplace.json, plugin.json, or openpackage.yml in ObservedWriteScope; five declare package.json for script/dependency edits only, not version bumps. CHANGELOG.md remains untouched and generated (D5.5).
Do not invent new event kinds. Do not document kinds that are not in KNOWN_KIND_STATE. Do not claim recover --fix emits terminal.

Evidence doctrine for the completeness regression: red-first — the check fails on today's skill (missing kinds), then passes after documentation. Measure denominators with their own commands when reporting counts (F12.2).

NonGoals.NonGoal: P1.10 skill emphasis inversion, approval lexicon, generated schema reference, or any other P1 authoring-surface restructuring. The minimal kind-set export in src/grace-cursor.ts is verification infrastructure for the completeness check only — it is not a license to restructure the skill or rewrite cursor protocol.
Evidence doctrine rewrites for ngrace-verification, ngrace-plan, or other skills beyond the minimum cross-reference if the plan needs a single pointer from execute to verification.
Anything in C-REPORT-HONESTY (P0.7, P0.9, F11, F14, F15, F16) or C-LEDGER-READ-ABSENCE (three-exit ledger reads).

Changing cursor protocol, fold validation, attempt-pair review severity, or fix-budget escalation behaviour. Expanding the grace-cursor export beyond the known-kind set (or a derived exhaustive list lockstep with KNOWN_KIND_STATE).
Fixing F9.6 (multi-task suite attribution) or F9.7 (pass-only invisibility) — those need per-task scope / schema, not skill prose. Documenting F9.8 only.

Any product version bump or edit to version surfaces (package.json version, README packaged-version line, openpackage.yml, marketplace.json, plugin.json). Hand-editing CHANGELOG.md (D5.5). Parsing grace-cursor.ts source text to discover kinds (F10).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-KIND-SET-DOCUMENTED: For every kind in the **exported** known-kind set at implementation HEAD (lockstep with KNOWN_KIND_STATE; currently 9 keys: opened, progress, resume, attempt, verification-unavailable, command-run, pause, terminal, escalation — denominator from the export, not from a skill substring scan), the execution skill documents that kind as protocol: when an agent should emit it and what it means. **A skill that merely contains the English word for a kind (e.g. "attempt", "pause", "resume") without a non-incidental documentation marker for that kind fails this criterion.** A check that scores documentation by counting substrings would accept today's skill at 4 of 9 and is wrong; only protocol markers counted against the exported set satisfy this criterion. After the change, the semantic gaps measured at authoring (**2 of 9** as protocol; pause/resume incidental English; five kinds absent) are closed.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-KIND-COMPLETENESS-TIED-TO-CODE: A regression in the suite **imports** the exported known-kind set from src/grace-cursor.ts (or a named export that is definitionally the keys of KNOWN_KIND_STATE) and asserts that every kind has a non-incidental documentation marker in skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md. **Adding a new key to KNOWN_KIND_STATE without updating the skill fails the suite.** **Parsing grace-cursor.ts (or any source file) with regex/AST greps to discover kinds fails this criterion** — that is the F10 shape (C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY T-005 completeness that matched call shapes and missed an entire namespace). A test that only asserts the string "terminal" (or any fixed string list disconnected from the export) appears in the skill also fails this criterion. How the marker is recognized is the plan's choice; coupling to the **exported** kind set without source-parsing is binding.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-TERMINAL-BEFORE-FOLD: The skill states that fold requires a terminal event inside the covering allocation (CLI enforces unterminated range otherwise), that the operator emits terminal (e.g. cursor advance --kind terminal) when the epoch's work is finished, and that recover --fix does not emit terminal. An agent who only read the skill before this change could not know that; after, they can without reading grace-cursor.ts. (F12.)
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ATTEMPT-ORDERING-F98: The skill states the operational ordering for honest red-first: write `ngrace cursor attempt --outcome fail` in its **own tool round trip**, then perform the production edit, then record pass — not in the same batched tool call as the fix. It attaches the reason: WriteEvidence digests ObservedWriteScope at attempt time, so a fail attempt batched with the fix cannot corroborate the sequence. It names the failure shape a reader will see: review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated on fail→pass pairs with no non-test digest movement, and that an honest disclosed gap is cheap while an unsubstantiated contradiction is not. **A criterion-satisfying edit that only inserts the words "round trip" or "F9.8" without the ordering rule, the digest reason, and the review failure shape fails this criterion.** (F9.8.)
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-MIRROR-BYTE-IDENTICAL: After the change, skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md and plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md are byte-identical (cmp / git diff --no-index clean). bun run ./scripts/validate-marketplace.ts reports no packaged-vs-canonical skill drift for ngrace-execute. Editing only one tree fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-NO-SKILL-REWRITE: The skill remains the execute workflow contract: preflight, assertion commands, mode selection, recovery table, execution rules, verdicts, calibration. This change **adds** protocol documentation (kinds, terminal fold, attempt ordering) and a **minimal** known-kind export in src/grace-cursor.ts for the completeness check. It does not invert skill emphasis into P1.10's "skills stop restating formats", does not replace the skill with a generated schema dump, does not restructure execution_rules into a different product, and does not absorb C-REPORT-HONESTY or other-skill rewrites. Touching src/grace-cursor.ts is not a license to rewrite cursor behaviour. A PR that restructures the skill beyond documenting the cursor protocol, or that expands the export beyond the kind set, fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-EXPORT-MINIMAL: The grace-cursor change is limited to exporting the known-kind set (or a derived exhaustive list lockstep with KNOWN_KIND_STATE) and tests of that export / completeness. No fold, attempt, recover, or gate behaviour changes. An implementation that refactors unrelated cursor code under cover of the export fails this criterion.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SUITE-AND-LINT: Completeness regression red before documentation, green after; remaining suite green; bun run ngrace lint --path . is 0 errors and 0 warnings; validate-marketplace green for skill mirror and version-surface sync (version surfaces unchanged by this bundle). No edits under docs/plans/archive/ or .ngrace/changes/archive/.

Manual or fixture read of skill sections for terminal-before-fold and attempt-ordering content against AC text. Existing V-M-CURSOR may cover the export test; no new V-M-* required for M-SKILLS (UTILITY without Path).
